request.spec:
A crew is now also a pool: it appears among the pools under its name, with the lead and the
members as its members at equal shares (100.00 split as patrons' shares are, the remainder on the
lead), and receives cuts like any pool. A pool cannot be added with a crew's name nor a crew with a
pool's name. Crew totals stay as they are.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A crew is now also a pool: it appears among the pools under its name, with the lead and the
members as its members at equal shares (100.00 split as patrons' shares are, the remainder on the
lead), and receives cuts like any pool. A pool cannot be added with a crew's name nor a crew with a
pool's name. Crew totals stay as they are.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every crew now also shows up as a pool under its own name and gets cuts like any other pool. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**How it works:**
- **Server (`PoolController`, `PoolService`):** the pools list now returns the sheet's real pools first, then each crew as a pool, both in the order they were added. A crew pool's members are its lead and then its members. Shares are split with the same rule as patrons' shares (`PersonService.patronShares`), so the remainder goes to the lead: for a crew of three that's 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33.
- **Nothing new is stored.** Crew pools are worked out from the crew each time the pools are read, so they always match the crew as it is now. That's why there's no database migration. To keep them from clashing with real pools, a crew pool's id is the crew's id made negative.
- **Name clashes:** adding a pool with a crew's name is refused, and so is adding a crew with a pool's name. Both show the form's usual error.
- **Cuts:** the existing cut maths (holds, retirement, remainder) needed no change, and crew totals are untouched.
- **Front end:**
  - Pools are re-read as soon as a crew or crew member is added, so the crew's pool appears without reloading the sheet.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Crew pools can't be edited from the Pools section.** I hid their "add member" form and left them out of the member choices for other pools, so a crew's membership is changed only through its crew. The request didn't say whether a crew pool can be a member of another pool. Say if you want that allowed.
- **Existing name clashes aren't fixed.** If a sheet already has a pool and a crew with the same name from before this change, nothing renames either one. Both would appear under that name.
